minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  August 17, 2021

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
August 17, 2021, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Pro Tem Morales called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:01
p.m.
The City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:
  Present:  Mayor Pro Tem Morales, Council Members Dotson,
  Padilla, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  Mayor Butts.
City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Angela Allen  Acting City Clerk
  Ken Campos  City Attorney

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEM. Mayor Pro Tem
Morales inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City
Council on the Closed Session Item Nos. CS-1, and CS-2.

There was no response.

Mayor Pro Tem Morales recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed
Session Item Nos. CS-1, and CS-2.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
hour of 2:00 p.m.
The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Dotson, Padilla,
  Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
follows:
  Aisha Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  David Esparza  Assistant City Manager/CFO *
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.
PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
item on the Agendas.
There was no response.

  1
   August 17, 2021

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  August 13, 2021, in the amount of $4,485,813.23 are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council
  Member Faulk that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on April 13, 2021,
  and April 13, 2021 (Special) be approved. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  FIRST AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. 21 – 061 APPROVED – WOW
  MEDIA, INC. Staff report dated August 17, 2021, was presented recommending
  approval of execution of the First Amendment to Billboard Lease and Development
  Agreement No. 21-061 with WOW Media, Inc. adding a fourth location near the
  intersection of South La Brea Avenue and Manchester Boulevard.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 21-061 with WOW Media, Inc.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  FIRST AMENDMENT TO AGREEEMENT NO. 21-141 APPROVED – J LEE
  ENGINEERING, INC., CALIFORNIA CODE SPECIALTIES, INC., AND THE
  CODE GROUP, INC., DBA AS VCA CODE. Staff report dated August 17, 2021, was
  presented recommending approval of the first amendment to Agreement No. 21-141 for
  Building Inspection consulting services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve the first amendment to Agreement No. 21-141 in
  an additional amount not to exceed $300,000 with the following consultants: 1) J Lee
  Engineering, Inc.; 2) California Code Specialties, Inc.; and 3) The Code Group, Inc., dba
  as VCA Code. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  FIRST AMENDMENT TO AGREEEMENT NO. 21-148 APPROVED – CSG
  CONSULTANTS, INC., INTERWEST CONSULTING GROUP, INC., AND J LEE
  ENGINEERING, INC.  Staff report dated August 17, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of the first amendment to Agreement No. 21-148 for Building
  Plan Check consulting services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve the first amendment to Agreement No. 21-148 in
  an additional amount not to exceed $200,000 with the following consultants: 1) CSG
  Consultants, Inc.; 2) Interwest Consulting Group, Inc.; and 3) J Lee Engineering, Inc.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
   August 17, 2021

171  AGREEMENT NO. 21-221 APPROVED – HISTORICAL SOCIETY OF
  CENTINELA VALLEY. Staff report dated August 17, 2021, was presented
  recommending approval of a 10-year lease agreement with Historical Society of
  Centinela Valley (Society) for $1 a year for use of certain historical buildings (Centinela
  Adobe Building, Land Office and Heritage Center), generally know and described as
  “The Centinela Adobe” located at 7634 Midfield Avenue, Los Angeles, California.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 21-221. The motion was carried
  out by following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Member Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO AGREEEMENT NO. 17-510 APPROVED –
  COMMUNITY VETERINARIAN HOSPITAL. Staff report dated August 17, 2021,
  was presented recommending approval of Amendment No. 2 to Agreement No. 17-510
  with Community Veterinarian Hospital, extending the term an additional one (1) year
  (covering the period from August 1, 2021 through July 31, 2022) to provide veterinary
  services for the Police Department.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 2 to Agreement No. 17-510, in
  an amount not to exceed $25,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – EVERBRIDGE. Staff report dated August 17, 2021,
  was presented recommending authorization of payment of the attached invoice submitted
  by Everbridge for Annual Remote Consulting Services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $18,000. The motion
  was carried out by following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Member Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  BID NO. RFB-0136 REJECTED – RENOVATION OF THE EMERGENCY
  OPERATIONS CENTER PROJECT. Staff report dated August 17, 2021, was
  presented recommending rejection of all bids submitted for the Renovation of the
  Emergency Operations Center Project, per Bid No. RFB-0136.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Reject all bids; and 2) Authorize staff to correct a
  procedural deficiency and rebid the project. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  AGREEMENT NO. 21-222 APPROVED – DEPARTMENT OF CALIFORNIA
  HIGHWAY PATROL; RESOLUTION NO. 21-135 ADOPTED – AMDENDING
  THE FISCAL YEAR BUDGET 2020-2021 BUDGET. Staff report dated August 17,
  2021, was presented recommending approval of a two-year agreement with the
  Department of California Highway Patrol (CHP) authorizing the Chief of Police (or
  designee) to request supplemental law enforcement services for special events from the
  CHP.

  MAYOR BUTTS COMMENTS. Mayor Butts commented to adopt Resolution No. 21-
  135 with the following provisions: 1) Approve Agreement No. 21-222 in the total amount
  not to exceed $8,000,000; 2) Adopt a resolution amending the Fiscal Year 2021
  expenditures and revenue in the amount of $500,000; and 3) Direct funds in the amount
  of $3.5 million for Fiscal Year 2023 along with commensurate revenues.

  3
   August 17, 2021

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 21-222 in the amount not to
  exceed $8,000,000; and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 21-135 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AGREEMENT WITH
  THE DEPARTMENT OF CALIFORNIA HIGHWAY PATROL IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $8,000,000

  with the following provisions: 1) Amend the Fiscal Year 2020-2021 expenditures and
  revenue in the amount of $500,000; 2) Direct said funds in an amount of 3.5 million
  dollars for Fiscal Year 2022-2023, and 4 (four) million dollars for Fiscal Year 2023-2024
  with commensurate revenue; and 3) Authorize the City Attorney, with the assistance of
  the Chief of Police to make modifications. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  ORDINANCE NO. 21-13 INTRODUCED – AMENDING THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE BY ADDING ARTICLE 7 TO CHAPTER 3 ESTABLISHING
  THE FORFEITURE OF NUISANCE VEHICLES ENGAGED IN SPEED
  CONTESTS OR EXHIBITIONS OF SPEED. Staff reported dated August 17, 2021,
  was presented recommending introduction of an ordinance amending the Inglewood
  Municipal Code by adding Article 7 to Chapter 3 to establish the forfeiture of nuisance
  vehicles engaged in motor vehicle speed contests or exhibitions of speed.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 21-13 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  ADDING ARTICLE 7 TO CHAPTER 3 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL
  CODE ESTABLISHING THE FORFEITURE OF NUISANCE VEHICLES
  ENGAGED IN MOTOR VEHICLE SPEED CONTESTS OR EXHIBITIONS OF
  SPEED

  was introduced by Mayor Butts.

178  ORDINANCE NO. 21-14 INTRODUCED – AMENDING THE INGLEWOOD
  MUNICIPAL CODE BY ADDING ARTICLE 8 TO CHAPTER 3 PROHIBITING
  SPECTATORS AT ILLEGAL MOTOR VEHICLE SPEED CONTESTS AND
  EXHIBITIONS OF SPEED. Staff report dated August 17, 2021, was presented
  recommending introduction of an ordinance amending the Inglewood Municipal Code by
  adding Article 8 to Chapter 3 to prohibit spectators at illegal motor vehicle speed contests
  and exhibitions of speed.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, Ordinance No. 21-14 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  ADDING ARTICLE 8 TO CHAPTER 3 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL
  CODE PROHIBITING SPECTATORS AT ILLEGAL MOTOR VEHICLE
  SPEED CONTESTS AND EXHIBITIONS OF SPEED

  4
   August 17, 2021

  was introduced by Mayor Butts.

  Inglewood Police Chief Mark Fronterotta introduced the presenters from the California
  Highway Patrol.

  Captain Muller, California Highway Patrol, and Officers with the California Highway
  Patrol Street Enforcement Unit presented a video presentation regarding intersection
  take-overs.

160  RESOLUTION NO. 21-136 ADOPTED – AMENDING THE MASTER FEE
  SCHEDULE TO ELIMINATE OVERDUE LIBRARY FINES AND APPROVE A
  DEBT FORGIVENESS PROGRAM.  Staff report dated August 17, 2021, was
  presented recommending adoption of a resolution amending the Master Fee Schedule to
  eliminate overdue library fines, and approve a debt forgiveness program for overdue fines
  and outstanding material costs.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  Resolution No. 21-136 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE MASTER FEE SCHEDULE TO
  ELIMINATE OVERDUE LIBRARY FINES AND APPROVE A DEBT
  FORGIVENESS PROGRAM FOR OVERDUE LIBRARY FINES AND
  OUTSTANDING MATERIAL COSTS

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  RESOLUTION NO. 21-137 ADOPTED – EXEMPTION FROM THE SURPLUS
  LAND ACT UNDER GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 54234(A)(1). Staff report
  dated August 17, 2021, was presented recommending adoption of a Resolution declaring
  as exempt from the Surplus Land Act under Government Code Section 54234(a)(1) all of
  the approximately 27 acres of land owned by the City and the City of Inglewood as
  Successor Agency to the Former Inglewood Redevelopment Agency, as identified in the
  Amended and Restated Exclusive Negotiation Agreement dated August 15, 2017, and
  also identified in the Disposition and Development Agreement dated September 15,
  2020, as the City Parcels.
